summary.text: An 18-year-old primigravida at 27.3 weeks of gestation attending a routine prenatal checkup was admitted to the emergency room with hypertension and lower limb edema. On the day of admission she reported chest pain and oral ulcers and had oxygen saturation 74% on room air. Examination showed respiratory distress, decreased breath sounds, generalized edema, erythematous fingertip lesions, ascites-type fluid waves and severe vulvar edema.

ICU admission showed elevated blood pressure, tachycardia, tachypnea, hypoxemia and anemia with low hemoglobin and hematocrit. Chest X-ray showed pulmonary edema, echocardiogram mild tricuspid regurgitation with posterior pericardial effusion, and Doppler ultrasound ruled out venous thrombosis. Skin histopathology confirmed discoid lupus. Antinuclear and anti-dsDNA antibodies were positive with low C3 and C4, proteinuria and a positive direct Coombs test.

Initial management included magnesium sulfate, antihypertensives, diuretics, corticosteroids for fetal lung maturation, albumin and antibiotics. A cesarean section was performed at 28 weeks of gestation for massive vulvar edema, delivering a neonate weighing 1100 grams with APGAR 7/8. Postpartum hemorrhage with uterine atony was managed with blood transfusions, a modified B-Lynch suture and a shock suit; steroid-induced hyperglycemia and a second episode of pulmonary edema followed.

After nephrology and rheumatology consultations the patient was diagnosed with new-onset SLE with lupus nephritis, discoid manifestations, severe preeclampsia and HELLP syndrome, two weeks after ICU admission. She was hospitalized for 56 days and discharged in stable condition on hydroxychloroquine and enalapril after placement of a subdermal contraceptive implant, with rheumatology follow-up arranged. Mother and infant stabilized.
